added_lemmas.statement: For a linear recursive structural equation model whose directed support is a rooted spanning tree and whose bidirected support is arbitrary, including bows, the randomized polynomial-time procedure of Gupta and Bl\"aser decides for every queried directed coefficient \(\lambda_e\) whether the generic queried-coordinate set has one value, two values, or infinitely many values. In each finite case it returns all corresponding \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions for the queried coefficient.

added_lemmas.statement: For every \(n\geq2\), the class \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) is exactly the rooted tree-shaped mixed-graph class with arbitrary bidirected support treated by the complete tree algorithm, up to the source paper's harmless vertex-count indexing convention. Consequently, on every input \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\), that algorithm returns the exact value \(d_e(G)\in\{1,2,\infty\}\) and, when \(d_e(G)<\infty\), all one or two \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions for \(\lambda_e\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\). By \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\), one has \(T\subseteq D\) and
\[
 |D\setminus T|\leq0.
\]
Cardinality is nonnegative, so \(D\setminus T=\varnothing\), whence \(D=T\). By \(\mathrm{ass:arborescence}\), this common edge set is a rooted spanning arborescence. Thus the entire directed support is a rooted spanning tree. The definition of \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) imposes no restriction on \(B\), so its bidirected support is arbitrary and may contain bows.

Conversely, given any rooted tree-shaped mixed graph on \(n\) vertices and any queried directed edge \(e\), put \(T=D\). Then \(T\) is a rooted spanning arborescence and \(|D\setminus T|=0\), so \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\). These two inclusions prove equality of the graph-query classes. A convention that counts nonroot vertices rather than all vertices merely shifts the displayed size index and changes no graph.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:gupta\mbox{-}blaser\mbox{-}tree\mbox{-}classification}\) to this common class. Suppose first that the published procedure returns \(m\in\{1,2\}\) generic values. By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), if \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\), its generic affine coordinate image over \(\overline{K_G}\) is exactly the root set of its minimal polynomial; if it is transcendental, that image is Zariski dense in \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\) and hence infinite. The returned finite set therefore implies algebraicity. If the minimal polynomial \(p\) had a repeated root, then \(\gcd(p,p')\neq1\). Irreducibility would force \(p\mid p'\), which is impossible because \(\deg p'<\deg p\) and \(p'\neq0\) in characteristic zero. Thus the minimal polynomial is separable, so its number of distinct roots equals its degree. Hence
\[
 d_e(G)=[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]=m.
\]
If the published procedure instead returns infinitely many generic values, algebraicity would contradict the finite root-set conclusion of the same incidence-localization theorem. Thus \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\) and \(d_e(G)=\infty\). The returned finite formulas are exactly the one or two \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions in the cited result. This is a transfer on the equal zero-excess class and makes no assertion for \(|D\setminus T|>0\).

added_lemmas.statement:
In the multihomogeneous system used by \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), the query component has at most \(n-1\) nonempty child blocks and its binary-factor graph is simple. For a simple graph on at most two blocks every prescribed-indegree coefficient is at most \(1\); on at most three blocks it is at most \(2\); and on at most four blocks it is at most \(4\), with
\[
 [X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq4}(X_i+X_j)=4.
\]
If \(n=5\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq1\), the coefficient is at most \(3\). Hence every finite queried-coordinate degree satisfies
\[
 d_e(G)\leq1\quad(n=3),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq2\quad(n=4),\qquad
 d_e(G)\leq3\quad(n=5,\ |D\setminus T|\leq1),
\]
and \(d_e(G)\leq4\) when \(n=5\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a finite simple graph \(H=(W,E_H)\) and a vector \(r=(r_v:v\in W)\) of nonnegative integers, define
\[
 c_H(r)=\left[\prod_{v\in W}X_v^{r_v}\right]
          \prod_{\{u,v\}\in E_H}(X_u+X_v).
\]
Choosing \(X_v\) from the factor indexed by \(\{u,v\}\) is the same as orienting that edge toward \(v\). Therefore \(c_H(r)\) is exactly the number of orientations of \(H\) having indegree vector \(r\). In particular it is zero unless
\[
 \sum_{v\in W}r_v=|E_H|,
 \qquad 0\leq r_v\leq\deg_H(v).
 \tag{1}
\]

If \(|W|\leq2\), simplicity gives at most one edge, and its orientation is fixed by its indegree vector. Thus \(c_H(r)\leq1\). If \(|W|\leq3\) and \(H\) is a forest, two distinct orientations with the same indegrees would have a nonempty balanced symmetric difference; following edges of that difference would produce a cycle, contrary to acyclicity. Hence the count is at most one. The only remaining graph is the triangle. Its two cyclic orientations both have indegree vector \((1,1,1)\), while every transitive orientation has a distinct labeled permutation of \((0,1,2)\). Hence the maximum on three blocks is two.

Now suppose \(|W|\leq4\). If \(|E_H|\leq4\), every connected component is a tree or there is exactly one unicyclic component: two independent cycle contributions in a simple graph on at most four vertices require at least five edges. In a tree attached to a cycle, the prescribed indegree at a leaf fixes its incident edge, and iterating from the leaves fixes every attached-tree edge. A cycle has at most its two cyclic orientations with the same remaining indegrees. Componentwise,
\[
 c_H(r)\leq2\qquad (|E_H|\leq4).
 \tag{2}
\]

For five edges, necessarily \(H=K_4\setminus\{1,2\}\). Directly expanding
\[
 P=(X_1+X_3)(X_1+X_4)(X_2+X_3)(X_2+X_4)(X_3+X_4)
\]
and fixing \((r_1,r_2)=(a,b)\in\{0,1,2\}^2\) gives the following maxima over the remaining two exponents:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
  &b=0&b=1&b=2\\ \hline
 a=0&1&2&1\\
 a=1&2&3&2\\
 a=2&1&2&1
 \end{array}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, choose the \(a\) factors among \(X_1+X_3,X_1+X_4\) that contribute \(X_1\), choose the \(b\) factors among \(X_2+X_3,X_2+X_4\) that contribute \(X_2\), and make either choice in \(X_3+X_4\); collecting equal exponent pairs gives (3). Thus every five-edge coefficient is at most three. When all four block capacities are positive, (1) forces a permutation of \((2,1,1,1)\); the coefficient is three when the exponent two is at vertex \(3\) or \(4\), and two when it is at vertex \(1\) or \(2\).

For six edges, \(H=K_4\). The possible sorted exponent patterns satisfying (1) are
\[
 (0,0,3,3),\quad(0,1,2,3),\quad(0,2,2,2),
 \quad(1,1,1,3),\quad(1,1,2,2).
\]
The first has coefficient zero because the edge joining the two zero-exponent vertices has no endpoint from which a variable may be chosen. A labeled vector of type \((0,1,2,3)\) has one transitive orientation. In types \((0,2,2,2)\) and \((1,1,1,3)\), the edges incident to the extreme vertex are forced and the remaining triangle has its two cyclic orientations. Finally, for \(r=(1,1,2,2)\), condition on the factor \(X_1+X_2\). If it contributes \(X_1\), the factors on edges \(13\) and \(14\) must contribute \(X_3X_4\), after which the triangle on \(2,3,4\) has two cyclic choices. The case in which it contributes \(X_2\) is symmetric. Therefore
\[
 [X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{i<j}(X_i+X_j)=2+2=4.
 \tag{4}
\]
This proves the four-block maximum and its attainment.

It remains to connect these counts to the SEM bound. In the square subsystem selected for \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), variables are blocked by child vertex. A rooted arborescence has one root, so there are at most \(n-1\) nonempty child blocks. The displayed formula for \(F_{ij}\) has degree at most one in the block for child \(i\), degree at most one in the block for child \(j\), and degree zero in every other block. An unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\) supplies at most its single residual \(F_{ij}\), so the binary-factor graph is simple. By \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\), the relevant B\'ezout coefficient is the orientation count just bounded.

For \(n=5\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq1\), the arborescence and excess budget give \(|D|\leq5\). A selected square subsystem therefore has at most five equations, hence at most five binary factors after unary factors are removed. With at most four binary factors, (2) gives the stronger bound two. With five binary factors there is no unary factor, all four blocks occur, and their positive capacities sum to five. The only capacity pattern is therefore a permutation of \((2,1,1,1)\), and (3) bounds its coefficient by three. Combining this with the two-, three-, and four-block bounds proves all displayed consequences for \(d_e(G)\).

added_lemmas.statement: Example 8 and Figure 5(b) of Foygel, Draisma, and Drton exhibit an acyclic five-vertex linear structural equation model whose directed support consists of five arrows and contains a rooted spanning arborescence, and whose generic covariance parametrization has degree three. Equivalently, its source function field is a degree-three extension of its covariance function field.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a graph-query \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,1}\) for which \(d_e(G)=3\). In particular,
\[
 D_1(5)\geq3,
\]
and one original directed coefficient separates the three characteristic-zero conjugate branches.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(\widetilde G\) be the graph in \(\mathrm{lem:foygel\mbox{-}five\mbox{-}node\mbox{-}degree\mbox{-}three}\). Its directed support has five arrows and contains a rooted spanning arborescence \(T\), which has four arrows on five vertices. Hence
\[
 |D\setminus T|=5-4=1,
\]
and \((\widetilde G,T,f)\in\mathcal G_{5,1}\) for every directed edge \(f\) of \(\widetilde G\).

Write \(K_{\widetilde G}\subset L_{\widetilde G}\) for the covariance and source function fields. The cited degree statement gives
\[
 [L_{\widetilde G}:K_{\widetilde G}]=3.
 \tag{5}
\]
For fixed \(\Sigma\) and \(\Lambda\), the noise matrix is not an additional fiber choice, because the covariance equation rearranges to
\[
 \Omega=(I_5-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_5-\Lambda).
 \tag{6}
\]
If every directed coordinate \(\lambda_f\) belonged to \(K_{\widetilde G}\), then (6) would put every allowed noise coordinate in \(K_{\widetilde G}\) as well. Since the source field is generated by the directed and allowed noise coordinates, this would give \(L_{\widetilde G}=K_{\widetilde G}\), contradicting (5). Thus some original directed edge \(e\) satisfies \(\lambda_e\notin K_{\widetilde G}\).

The tower law and (5) give
\[
 [K_{\widetilde G}(\lambda_e):K_{\widetilde G}]
 \mid [L_{\widetilde G}:K_{\widetilde G}]=3.
\]
The left side is greater than one, so primality of three forces it to equal three. Therefore \(d_e(\widetilde G)=3\), proving the lower bound. If its minimal polynomial \(p\) were inseparable, irreducibility would give \(p\mid p'\); this is impossible because \(p'\neq0\) in characteristic zero and \(\deg p'<\deg p\). By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), the three distinct roots are exactly the generic affine queried-coordinate image, so this original edge coordinate separates all three conjugate branches.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(G^{(4)}=(V,D,B)\) have \(V=\{0,1,2,3,4\}\),
\[
 D=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,2\to3,1\to4,2\to4\},
 \qquad
 B=\{0\leftrightarrow i:1\leq i\leq4\},
\]
let
\[
 T=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,1\to4\},
 \qquad e=2\to4,
\]
and write \(f=\lambda_e\). Then \((G^{(4)},T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\) and \(d_e(G^{(4)})=4\). More precisely, at the rational positive-definite covariance \(\Sigma^{\star}\) displayed in the proof, the residual fiber has four reduced points with distinct real \(f\)-coordinates, namely the roots of
\[
 q(f)=(f-7)\bigl(8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2
 +1271943861499f-2976933819575\bigr).
\]
Every root extends to real directed coefficients and a positive-definite disturbance matrix \(\Omega\) having the required missing-bidirected zero pattern. For every \(N\geq5\), appending \(N-5\) fully bidirected children of \(0\) and placing their arrows in \(T\) preserves the queried-coordinate degree four. Consequently \(D_k(5)\geq4\) for every admissible \(k\geq2\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The displayed \(T\) has four edges, gives every nonroot vertex exactly one parent, and has a directed path from \(0\) to every vertex. It is therefore a rooted spanning arborescence. Moreover,
\[
 D\setminus T=\{2\to3,2\to4\},
\]
the order \(0<1<2<3<4\) is topological for \(D\), and \(e\in D\). Thus \((G^{(4)},T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\).

Put
\[
 (a,b,c,d,u,f)
 =\bigl(\lambda_{01},\lambda_{02},\lambda_{13},
         \lambda_{23},\lambda_{14},\lambda_{24}\bigr).
\]
At the rational source point
\[
 (a,b,c,d,u,f)=(2,3,4,5,6,7),
 \qquad
 \Omega^{\star}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 30&1&2&3&4\\
 1&31&0&0&0\\
 2&0&32&0&0\\
 3&0&0&33&0\\
 4&0&0&0&34
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
the disturbance support is exactly allowed by \(B\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R^5\), the inequality \(2|x_i x_j|\leq x_i^2+x_j^2\) gives
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{\star}x
 \geq20x_0^2+30x_1^2+30x_2^2+30x_3^2+30x_4^2>0
\]
for \(x\neq0\). Hence \(\Omega^{\star}\) is positive definite. Direct multiplication in the defining covariance parametrization gives
\[
 \Sigma^{\star}=(I_5-\Lambda^{\star})^{-\mathsf T}
 \Omega^{\star}(I_5-\Lambda^{\star})^{-1}
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 30&61&92&707&1014\\
 61&155&187&1561&2247\\
 92&187&314&2327&3332\\
 707&1561&2327&17981&25747\\
 1014&2247&3332&25747&36972
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Because \(I_5-\Lambda^{\star}\) is unit triangular in the displayed topological order, it is invertible; congruence also shows directly that \(\Sigma^{\star}\) is positive definite.

The only missing bidirected pairs are the six pairs among \(\{1,2,3,4\}\). Substitution of (7) into their six residual polynomials gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 r_{12}&=30ab-92a-61b+187,\\
 r_{13}&=61ac+92ad-707a-155c-187d+1561,\\
 r_{14}&=61au+92af-1014a-155u-187f+2247,\\
 r_{23}&=61bc+92bd-707b-187c-314d+2327,\\
 r_{24}&=61bu+92bf-1014b-187u-314f+3332,\\
 r_{34}&=155cu+187cf-2247c+187du+314df-3332d\\
 &\hspace{2.8em}{}-1561u-2327f+25747.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{8}
\]
Exact Buchberger reduction over \(\mathbb Q\), in lexicographic order \(a>b>c>d>u>f\), gives the following basis of \(J^{\star}=(r_{12},r_{13},r_{14},r_{23},r_{24},r_{34})\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
 g_a={}&384915840a+425450175590061f^3-8965411803407607f^2\\
 &{}+62974399432228195f-147445028655847225,\\
 g_b={}&741827520b-593375419233f^3+12321625507347f^2\\
 &{}-85271405126447f+196665729339485,\\
 g_c={}&615040c+25798931271f^3-543666188277f^2\\
 &{}+3818873142057f-8941504654939,\\
 g_d={}&4d-3f+1,\\
 g_u={}&153760u+8599643757f^3-181222062759f^2\\
 &{}+1272957714019f-2980501654153,\\
 g_f={}&8599643757f^4-241347527724f^3+2539994011474f^2\\
 &{}-11880540850068f+20838536737025.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{9}
\]
This is an exact two-sided ideal certificate: exact multivariate division gives
\[
 \operatorname{rem}_{(g_a,g_b,g_c,g_d,g_u,g_f)}(r_{ij})=0
 \quad(1\leq i<j\leq4),
 \tag{10}
\]
reverse division expresses every \(g_{\bullet}\) as an element of the ideal generated by the six polynomials in (8), and every pairwise Buchberger \(S\)-polynomial of the list (9) reduces to zero. Thus the ideals generated by (8) and (9) are equal, rather than merely having the same eliminant. The last basis element factors as
\[
 g_f=q(f)=(f-7)c(f),
\]
where
\[
 c(f)=8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2
       +1271943861499f-2976933819575.
\]
Exact integer arithmetic gives
\[
 c(7)=-30256,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{disc}(c)
 =1802165059445823134111101206528>0.
 \tag{11}
\]
To see directly what the sign in (11) implies, write the roots of a real cubic with leading coefficient \(A\) as \(r_1,r_2,r_3\). Its discriminant is
\[
 A^4\prod_{i<j}(r_i-r_j)^2.
\]
If it had only one real root \(r\), the other two would be \(u+iv\) and \(u-iv\) with \(v\neq0\), and the displayed product would equal
\[
 -4A^4v^2\bigl((r-u)^2+v^2\bigr)^2<0.
\]
The positive discriminant in (11) therefore forces three distinct real roots. The first equality in (11) shows that none equals \(7\). Thus \(q\) has four distinct real roots. Since the leading coefficients of \(g_a,g_b,g_c,g_d,g_u\) in their respective non-\(f\) variables are nonzero rational integers, each root of \(q\) determines exactly one real value of each of \(a,b,c,d,u\). Consequently
\[
 \mathbb C[a,b,c,d,u,f]/J^{\star}
 \cong\mathbb C[f]/(q)
 \cong\mathbb C^4.
 \tag{12}
\]
Thus the specialized residual fiber consists of four reduced points with pairwise distinct real \(f\)-coordinates. The original source point is the point with \(f=7\), so the fiber is nonempty.

At each point of the reduced zero-dimensional complete intersection (12), the residual Jacobian with respect to \((a,b,c,d,u,f)\) has rank six. To pass from the specialization to the generic fiber without relying on upper semicontinuity alone, write the fifteen symmetric covariance coordinates as \(s=\Sigma^{\star}+z\) and denote the six-residual map by \(R(s,v)\), where \(v=(a,b,c,d,u,f)\). At any one of the four points \(v_0\), seek a formal solution
\[
 v(z)=v_0+\sum_{r\geq1}v_r(z),
\]
with \(v_r\) homogeneous of degree \(r\) in \(z\). The homogeneous degree-\(r\) equation is
\[
 \left.\frac{\partial R}{\partial v}\right|_{(\Sigma^{\star},v_0)}v_r
 =-H_r(v_1,\ldots,v_{r-1};z),
 \tag{13}
\]
where the right side is determined by lower degrees. The invertible Jacobian gives a unique \(v_r\) at every step. Hence all four reduced points lift to formal branches over \(\mathbb C[[z]]\), and their \(f\)-series remain distinct because their constant terms are distinct.

The incidence space is irreducible by \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\). Concretely, the acyclic polynomial change of coordinates
\[
 \Omega=(I_5-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_5-\Lambda)
\]
has a polynomial inverse, and the six missing-noise conditions set six independent \(\Omega\)-coordinates to zero. The source dimension is
\[
 |D|+|B|+|V|=6+4+5=15,
\]
equal to the dimension of the symmetric covariance space. The formal sections (13) show that the covariance projection is dominant and generically zero-dimensional; therefore \(P_G=(0)\), \(K_G=\mathbb C(s)\), and the generic full-fiber degree is at least four.

For the upper bound, partition the six variables into the four blocks
\[
 A=(a),\qquad B_0=(b),\qquad C=(c,d),\qquad U_0=(u,f),
\]
of sizes \((1,1,2,2)\). Each residual indexed by a pair of distinct blocks has degree at most one in each of those blocks. By \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\) and equation (4), the generic full fiber has at most four isolated points counted with multiplicity. It therefore has degree exactly four. The four formal embeddings have distinct images of \(f\), so
\[
 [K_G(f):K_G]\geq4.
\]
Coordinate degree cannot exceed full-fiber degree; hence
\[
 d_{\,2\to4}(G^{(4)})=4.
 \tag{14}
\]
The exact \(S_G\)-localization in \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) inverts no directed-coordinate expression, so (14) concerns the source-prime generic queried projection and loses none of these finite values.

It remains to check the claimed real positive-definite lifting. Each real root of \(q\) gives real \((a,b,c,d,u)\) through (9), hence a real acyclic coefficient matrix \(\widetilde\Lambda\). Define
\[
 \widetilde\Omega=(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}
 \Sigma^{\star}(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda).
 \tag{15}
\]
Equations (8) are exactly the six missing-bidirected entries of (15), so \(\widetilde\Omega_{ij}=0\) for every \(i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\). The order \(0<1<2<3<4\) makes \(I_5-\widetilde\Lambda\) unit triangular and therefore invertible. Since \(\Sigma^{\star}\succ0\), congruence in (15) gives \(\widetilde\Omega\succ0\). Thus every one of the four real roots has a complete real, support-valid, positive-definite lift; no uniqueness assertion is inferred from this fact.

Finally, append a new vertex \(w\) with the sole directed edge \(0\to w\), place that edge in \(T\), and put every bidirected pair incident with \(w\) into \(B\). There is no new missing-bidirected residual involving \(w\), so the old residuals are unchanged. Let \(L_0\) and \(K_0\) be the old source and covariance fields, let \(x=\lambda_{0w}\), let \(\eta\) collect the newly allowed noise coordinates, and let \(z=(\sigma_{iw}:i\in V)\) together with \(\sigma_{ww}\). For fixed old source coordinates and \(x\), the covariance congruence gives a triangular polynomial change with polynomial inverse between \(\eta\) and \(z\). Therefore
\[
 L_1=L_0(x,z),\qquad K_1=K_0(z),
\]
where \(x\) and the entries of \(z\) are algebraically independent over \(L_0\). To verify degree preservation directly, choose a \(K_0\)-basis \(b_1,\ldots,b_4\) of \(K_0(f)\). If
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^4 r_i(z)b_i=0,\qquad r_i(z)\in K_0(z),
\]
then clearing denominators and comparing coefficients of the algebraically independent monomials in \(z\) gives a \(K_0\)-linear relation among the \(b_i\) for every monomial. Every coefficient is therefore zero, so all \(r_i\) vanish. The same basis spans \(K_0(z)(f)\) over \(K_0(z)\), because every power of \(f\) reduces in the old basis. Thus
\[
 [K_1(f):K_1]=[K_0(f):K_0]=4.
\]
Iteration proves the appending claim. At \(n=5\), the class inclusion \(\mathcal G_{5,2}\subseteq\mathcal G_{5,k}\) for \(k\geq2\) gives \(D_k(5)\geq4\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible pair with \(2\leq n\leq5\), the exact sharp coordinate-degree frontier is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 n & D_k(n)\\ \hline
 2 & D_0(2)=1,\\
 3 & D_k(3)=1\quad(0\leq k\leq1),\\
 4 & D_k(4)=2\quad(0\leq k\leq3),\\
 5 & D_0(5)=2,\quad D_1(5)=3,\quad D_k(5)=4\quad(2\leq k\leq6).
\end{array}
\]
In each nontrivial lower-bound construction an original directed coefficient separates all generic conjugate branches.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The admissible range is \(0\leq k\leq(n-1)(n-2)/2\). For \(n=2\), this forces \(k=0\), and \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) gives \(D_0(2)=1\).

For \(n=3\), one has \(k\in\{0,1\}\). The two-block conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:small\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maxima}\) gives \(d_e(G)\leq1\) for every finite query in either class. Since every triple with zero excess also belongs to every larger admissible budget class,
\[
 \mathcal G_{3,0}\subseteq\mathcal G_{3,k}.
\]
Together with the tree witness \(D_0(3)=1\) from \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\), this gives the reverse inequality. Hence \(D_k(3)=1\).

For \(n=4\), the three-block bound gives \(d_e(G)\leq2\) for every finite query and every admissible \(k\). The inclusion \(\mathcal G_{4,0}\subseteq\mathcal G_{4,k}\) and the separating degree-two tree witness in \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}maxima\mbox{-}support}\) give \(D_k(4)\geq2\). Thus \(D_k(4)=2\) for \(0\leq k\leq3\).

For \(n=5,k=0\), the tree result gives \(D_0(5)=2\). For \(k=1\), the special five-edge bound in \(\mathrm{lem:small\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}maxima}\) gives \(D_1(5)\leq3\), while \(\mathrm{lem:five\mbox{-}node\mbox{-}cubic\mbox{-}coordinate\mbox{-}transfer}\) supplies a graph and an original edge of degree three. Hence \(D_1(5)=3\). added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 j=\min\{k,\lfloor(n-4)/2\rfloor\}.
\]
Then \(j\leq k\) and \(n\geq2j+4\). Apply \(\mathrm{thm:large\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\) with excess budget \(j\). The one-sink graph \(G^{\star}_{j,n}\) belongs to \(\mathcal G_{n,j}\), and its original edge \(e^{\star}\) satisfies
\[
 d_{e^{\star}}(G^{\star}_{j,n})=2^{j+1}.
\]
Because an input with at most \(j\) excess arrows also has at most \(k\) excess arrows, \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal G_{n,j}\subseteq\mathcal G_{n,k}.
\]
Therefore \(D_k(n)\geq2^{j+1}\). For every integer \(n\geq4\),
\[
 \lfloor(n-4)/2\rfloor+1=\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor,
\]
and hence
\[
 j+1=\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}.
\]
Substitution proves the displayed envelope. The final five-vertex values follow independently from \(\mathrm{thm:small\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\), and are stated separately because they exceed the one-sink envelope there.

Let
\[

T=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,1\to4\},

\[
d_e(G)=4.
\]
At the rational covariance
\[
\Sigma_\star=
\begin{pmatrix}
30&61&92&707&1014\\
61&155&187&1561&2247\\
92&187&314&2327&3332\\
707&1561&2327&17981&25747\\
1014&2247&3332&25747&36972

\]

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write
\[
a=\lambda_{01},\quad b=\lambda_{02},\quad c=\lambda_{13},\quad
d=\lambda_{23},\quad u=\lambda_{14},\quad f=\lambda_{24}.
\]
The set \(T\) has root \(0\), gives every other vertex exactly one parent, and has four edges. Hence it is a rooted spanning arborescence. Moreover \(D\setminus T=\{2\to3,2\to4\}\), so \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{5,2}\) by \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\).

First construct a regular real specialization. Set
\[
(a,b,c,d,u,f)=(2,3,4,5,6,7)
\]
and let \(\Omega_\star\) have diagonal \((30,31,32,33,34)\), entries \((\Omega_\star)_{0i}=i\) for \(1\le i\le4\), and all other off-diagonal entries zero. For every nonzero \(x\in\mathbb R^5\), the inequality \(2|x_ix_j|\le x_i^2+x_j^2\) gives
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\Omega_\star x
\ge \sum_{i=0}^4\left((\Omega_\star)_{ii}
-\sum_{j\ne i}|(\Omega_\star)_{ij}|\right)x_i^2>0,
\]
because the five parenthesized margins are \(20,30,30,30,30\). Thus \(\Omega_\star\succ0\). Direct multiplication in
\(\Sigma=(I_5-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega_\star(I_5-\Lambda)^{-1}\) gives exactly the displayed matrix \(\Sigma_\star\).

The missing bidirected pairs are precisely the six pairs inside \(\{1,2,3,4\}\). Therefore the specialization of the incidence ideal is generated in \(\mathbb Q[a,b,c,d,u,f]\) by
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_1={}&30ab-92a-61b+187,\\
R_2={}&61ac+92ad-707a-155c-187d+1561,\\
R_3={}&61au+92af-1014a-155u-187f+2247,\\
R_4={}&61bc+92bd-707b-187c-314d+2327,\\
R_5={}&61bu+92bf-1014b-187u-314f+3332,\\
R_6={}&155cu+187cf-2247c+187du+314df-3332d\\
&\hspace{2.8em}-1561u-2327f+25747.
\end{aligned}
\]
These are the entries of \((I_5-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_\star(I_5-\Lambda)\) at those six missing pairs, so their vanishing is equivalent to the required off-diagonal zero pattern.

We next give the characteristic-zero elimination certificate. In lexicographic order
\(a>b>c>d>u>f\), exact Buchberger reduction over \(\mathbb Q\) gives the following basis; harmless nonzero rational normalizing constants have been suppressed:
\[
\begin{aligned}
H_1={}&384915840a+425450175590061f^3-8965411803407607f^2\\
&+62974399432228195f-147445028655847225,\\
H_2={}&741827520b-593375419233f^3+12321625507347f^2\\
&-85271405126447f+196665729339485,\\
H_3={}&615040c+25798931271f^3-543666188277f^2\\
&+3818873142057f-8941504654939,\\
H_4={}&4d-3f+1,\\
H_5={}&153760u+8599643757f^3-181222062759f^2\\
&+1272957714019f-2980501654153,\\
H_6={}&q(f)=(f-7)c(f),\\
c(f)={}&8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2
+1271943861499f-2976933819575.
\end{aligned}
\]
For completeness, this is a two-sided ideal certificate rather than a one-way eliminant: each \(H_j\) is obtained from the \(R_i\) by exact rational \(S\)-polynomial reductions, while direct division of every \(R_i\) by \((H_1,\ldots,H_6)\) has zero remainder. Hence
\[
(R_1,\ldots,R_6)=(H_1,\ldots,H_6).
\]
The leading monomials of the normalized \(H_j\) are respectively
\(a,b,c,d,u,f^4\); they are pairwise relatively prime, so Buchberger's product criterion also verifies that all remaining \(S\)-polynomials reduce to zero. This proves both ideal containments and the asserted lexicographic basis over characteristic zero.

The displayed basis identifies the specialized quotient with \(\mathbb Q[f]/(q)\), since \(H_1,\ldots,H_5\) recover exactly one value of \((a,b,c,d,u)\) from each value of \(f\). Exact integer arithmetic gives
\[
c(7)=-30256
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{disc}(c)
=1802165059445823134111101206528>0.
\]
The nonzero discriminant says that the cubic has no repeated root. A real cubic has either three real roots or one real root and a nonreal conjugate pair; from the product formula for its discriminant, the latter case has negative discriminant. Thus \(c\) has three distinct real roots. Since \(c(7)\ne0\), these roots and \(7\) are four distinct real roots of \(q\). It follows that the specialized incidence fiber is a reduced set of four points with pairwise distinct original-coordinate values \(f=\lambda_{24}\).

We now pass from the specialization to the generic coordinate degree. Partition the six coefficient variables into the four incoming-vertex blocks
\[
\{a\},\qquad\{b\},\qquad\{c,d\},\qquad\{u,f\}.
\]
The six residuals have binary block graph \(K_4\) and degree one in each incident block. The multihomogeneous coefficient in \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\) is
\[
[X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{1\le i<j\le4}(X_i+X_j)=4.
\]
Indeed, in the factor order \(12,13,14,23,24,34\), the only four choices of a variable with exponent vector \((1,1,2,2)\) are
\[
\begin{gathered}
(1,3,4,2,4,3),\qquad(1,3,4,3,2,4),\\
(2,1,4,3,4,3),\qquad(2,3,1,3,4,4).
\end{gathered}
\]
Consequently every isolated generic solution, counted with multiplicity, contributes to a total of at most four.

It remains to justify that the four specialized points are genuine generic branches. Since their fiber algebra is reduced and zero-dimensional, its cotangent space at every point is zero. The six \(R_i\) generate the fiber ideal in six variables, so their Jacobian with respect to \((a,b,c,d,u,f)\) has rank six at each point. Equivalently, this also follows by differentiating the triangular basis above, whose diagonal derivatives in \((a,b,c,d,u)\) are nonzero and whose last derivative is \(q'(f)\ne0\). For covariance deviations \(z\), expand the residual equations degree by degree in a putative series \(\lambda(z)\). At degree one the invertible Jacobian determines the coefficient uniquely; after degrees below \(r\) have been determined, the degree-\(r\) equation has the same Jacobian and hence uniquely determines the degree-\(r\) coefficient. This constructs four distinct formal solution branches over \(\mathbb C[[z]]\), and their \(f\)-series remain distinct because their constant terms are distinct.

The graph has six directed coefficients, five disturbance variances, and four supported off-diagonal disturbance coordinates, hence fifteen source coordinates, equal to the fifteen covariance coordinates. The existence of any one full-rank formal inverse makes the covariance parametrization dominant; thus its covariance function field is embedded by the independent covariance deviations. By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), the generic queried-coordinate image is the root set of the minimal polynomial of \(f\). The four formal branches give four distinct roots of that polynomial, so \(d_e(G)\ge4\). The multihomogeneous bound just proved gives \(d_e(G)\le4\), and therefore
\[
d_e(G)=4.
\]
This argument concerns the original coefficient \(\lambda_{24}\), not merely a primitive element for the whole fiber.

Every one of the four roots is real, and the five triangular recovery equations have real coefficients and nonzero constant multipliers; hence every root gives a real matrix \(\Lambda_j\). Define
\[
\Omega_j=(I_5-\Lambda_j)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_\star(I_5-\Lambda_j).
\]
Acyclicity makes \(I_5-\Lambda_j\) unit triangular in the order \(0,1,2,3,4\), hence invertible. For nonzero real \(x\),
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\Omega_jx
=\bigl((I_5-\Lambda_j)x\bigr)^{\mathsf T}
\Sigma_\star\bigl((I_5-\Lambda_j)x\bigr)>0,
\]
because \(\Sigma_\star\succ0\), itself following from its congruence with \(\Omega_\star\succ0\). Thus \(\Omega_j\succ0\). The six residual equations say exactly that all off-diagonal entries missing from \(B\) vanish, so all four real roots have supported positive-definite lifts.

Finally append one new vertex \(w\) as a child of \(0\), put \(0\to w\) into \(T\), and allow every bidirected pair incident to \(w\). There is then no new missing-pair residual involving \(w\). Over the old source field, congruence by \(I-\Lambda\) is an invertible linear change between the new disturbance row and the new covariance row; the new arrow coefficient is an additional free transcendental. Hence the enlarged source field can be written
\[
L'=L(\lambda_{0w},\sigma_{iw}:i\in V,\sigma_{ww}),
\]
while the enlarged covariance field is
\[
K'_G=K_G(\sigma_{iw}:i\in V,\sigma_{ww}),
\]
with all displayed adjoining variables algebraically independent over the respective old fields. Irreducibility of the old minimal polynomial is preserved by a purely transcendental base extension, so
\[
[K'_G(\lambda_e):K'_G]=[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]=4.
\]
Iteration proves the appending claim. For \(n=5\), the same graph belongs to \(\mathcal G_{5,k}\) whenever admissible \(k\ge2\), since its excess is two. The definition of \(D_k(5)\) therefore yields \(D_k(5)\ge4\).

proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
r=|D\setminus T|.
\]
Because \(r\) is read directly from the supplied graph, dispatching on \(r=0\) or \(r>0\) is deterministic and exhaustive.

Suppose first that \(r=0\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}algorithm\mbox{-}transfer}\), the graph is in exactly the published tree-shaped mixed-graph class, including arbitrary bidirected support.  Run the transferred tree algorithm with failure tolerance \(\delta\).  If \(d_e(G)<\infty\), that lemma proves
\[
d_e(G)\in\{1,2\}
\]
and proves that its returned list \((\rho_i)_{i=1}^{d_e(G)}\) exhausts the generic complex coordinate values.  The dispatcher therefore returns
\[
(\operatorname{tree},d_e(G),(\rho_i)_{i=1}^{d_e(G)}).
\]
If \(d_e(G)=\infty\), the same lemma proves that the published procedure reports the infinite case, and the dispatcher returns \((\operatorname{tree},\infty)\).  These are the first two stated outputs, with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\).

It remains to analyze \(r>0\).  Put
\[
u=(\lambda_D,\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
N=|D|+|B|+n,
\]
so that, by the definition of \(L\),
\[
L=\mathbb C(u_1,\ldots,u_N).
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:acyclic}\), there is a topological ordering in which \(\Lambda\) is strictly triangular.  Thus \(\Lambda^n=0\), and direct multiplication gives
\[
(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}=I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}.
\]
Consequently every entry of \((I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\) is a polynomial of degree at most \(n-1\) in \(\lambda_D\).  Since every entry of \(\Omega\) is linear in \((\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}})\), each distinct covariance coordinate
\[
s_{ij}(u):=\phi_G(\sigma_{ij})
=\bigl[(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\bigr]_{ij}
\]
is a polynomial of total degree at most
\[
(n-1)+1+(n-1)=2n-1.
\]
Repeated matrix multiplication constructs all these polynomials by arithmetic circuits of size polynomial in \(n\).

Let \(s=(s_{ij}:i\leq j)\), let \(J_0=\partial s/\partial u\), and let \(J_1\) be obtained by adjoining to \(J_0\) the row \(\partial\lambda_e/\partial u\).  The entries of \(J_0\) have degree at most \(2n-2\), and the added row has degree zero.

We prove the rank criterion used by the dispatcher.  Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in L\), set \(F=\mathbb C(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\), and choose a maximal algebraically independent subfamily \(b_1,\ldots,b_q\) of the \(a_i\).  Then \(b_1,\ldots,b_q\) is a transcendence basis of \(F/\mathbb C\).  Extend it by \(c_1,\ldots,c_ell\) to a transcendence basis of \(L/\mathbb C\).  Since \(L\) is finitely generated, the extension
\[
L/\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_q,c_1,\ldots,c_ell)
\]
is finite algebraic, and it is separable because the characteristic is zero.

For each \(j\), the derivation of the displayed rational-function field that sends \(b_j\) to \(1\) and all other \(b\)'s and \(c\)'s to zero extends uniquely to \(L\).  Indeed, if \(v\) is algebraic with minimal polynomial \(g(t)=\sum_h g_h t^h\), differentiating \(g(v)=0\) forces
\[
g'(v)\,dv=-\sum_h v^h\,d g_h,
\]
and separability gives \(g'(v)\neq0\).  Applying the extended derivations to any relation \(\sum_j q_j\,db_j=0\), with \(q_j\in L\), yields \(q_j=0\) for every \(j\).  Thus \(db_1,\ldots,db_q\) are linearly independent over \(L\).

Conversely, each \(a_i\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_q)\).  Differentiating its separable minimal polynomial expresses \(da_i\) in the \(L\)-span of \(db_1,\ldots,db_q\).  Since the \(b_j\) themselves are among the \(a_i\), we conclude
\[
\dim_L\operatorname{span}_L\{da_1,\ldots,da_m\}
=q
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}F.
\]

Apply this identity first to the covariance polynomials and then to those polynomials together with \(\lambda_e\).  The rows of the two Jacobians are the coordinate vectors of the corresponding differentials in the basis \(du_1,\ldots,du_N\).  Using the definition \(K_G=\mathbb C(s_{ij}:i,j\in V)\), we obtain
\[
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G,
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G(\lambda_e).
\]
Adjoining one element raises transcendence degree by zero precisely when that element is algebraic and otherwise raises it by one.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1=\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda_e\text{ is algebraic over }K_G,
\]
whereas \(\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1=\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0+1\) is equivalent to transcendence.

The dispatcher evaluates both Jacobians at independently sampled exact source points and computes their ranks by exact Gaussian elimination.  There are at most \(n(n+1)/2+1\leq n^2+1\) rows and at most
\[
N=|D|+|B|+n\leq n(n-1)+n=n^2
\]
columns.  Hence every relevant minor has size at most \(n^2+1\) and total degree at most
\[
(n^2+1)(2n-2)\leq2n^3.
\]
Choose every source coordinate independently and uniformly from a finite rational set \(S\) with
\[
|S|\geq \left\lceil\frac{4n^3}{\delta}\right\rceil.
\]
An evaluated rank never exceeds the generic rank.  If the evaluated rank is smaller, a fixed nonzero generic maximal minor has vanished at the sampled point.  By \(\mathrm{lem:schwartz\mbox{-}zippel\mbox{-}bound}\), this event has probability at most
\[
\frac{2n^3}{|S|}\leq\frac{\delta}{2}
\]
for each Jacobian.  A union bound shows that both evaluated ranks equal their generic ranks with probability at least \(1-\delta\).  On this event the displayed rank criterion gives the correct algebraic or transcendental tag.  The exact evaluation points, pivot positions, and nonzero evaluated pivot minors form the transcript \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\).

If the augmented rank is larger, then \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\), so the homomorphism
\[
K_G[t]\longrightarrow A_K,
\qquad
t\longmapsto\lambda_e,
\]
is injective.  By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), \(A_K\) is an integral \(K_G\)-algebra with fraction field \(L\).  The injection therefore induces a dominant morphism
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(A_K)\longrightarrow\mathbb A^1_{K_G}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\dim A_K
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{K_G}\operatorname{Frac}(A_K)
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{K_G}L\geq1,
\]
because \(L\) contains \(\lambda_e\), which is transcendental over \(K_G\).  The augmented pivot minor together with the two rank transcripts is thus the asserted dominance certificate \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\), and the fourth output is correct.

If the ranks agree, then \(d_e(G)<\infty\).  The already established \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) gives
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^{|D|-n+2}\leq2^{k+1}.
\]
Thus the third output is correct.  This step supplies only a degree ceiling: neither the rank computation nor the bound constructs \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\).

Finally, the tree branch is randomized polynomial time by \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}algorithm\mbox{-}transfer}\).  On the positive-excess branch, nilpotent matrix summation, circuit differentiation, exact evaluations, and Gaussian elimination require polynomially many arithmetic operations and transcript entries in \(n\).  Sampling uses \(O(\log n+\log(1/\delta))\) bits per coordinate, with bit complexity charged separately in \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\).  Since \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\), one universal \(C>0\) bounds both branch complexities by
\[
n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)).
\]
Only one branch is executed, so its error probability is the dispatcher's total error probability.  This proves all four cases and the stated complexity and certificate-length bounds.

added_lemmas.statement: For every tree-shaped acyclic mixed graph whose directed component is a rooted directed tree and whose bidirected support is unrestricted, and for every queried directed coefficient, the Gupta--Bl\"aser Algorithm 2 is a randomized polynomial-time procedure that decides whether the generic coordinate-value set has cardinality one, cardinality two, or is infinite; no other case occurs.  In the two finite cases it returns, respectively, one or two corresponding fractional affine square-root terms of covariance polynomials.  For every \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the polynomial-identity-test sampling sets can be chosen so that the total error probability is at most \(\eta\).

added_lemmas.statement: For every \(n\geq 2\), the graph part of \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) is exactly the class of tree-shaped mixed graphs treated by Gupta--Bl\"aser, with their \(n+1\)-vertex indexing replaced by the present \(n\)-vertex indexing: \(D=T\) is a rooted spanning arborescence and \(B\) is arbitrary.  For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\), their randomized polynomial-time algorithm therefore returns either \((\operatorname{tree},d_e(G),(\rho_i)_{i=1}^{d_e(G)})\), where \(d_e(G)\in\{1,2\}\) and the returned fractional affine square-root terms \(\rho_i\) exhaust the generic complex values of \(\lambda_e\), or \((\operatorname{tree},\infty)\), in which case \(d_e(G)=\infty\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\), \(T\subseteq D\) and \(|D\setminus T|\leq0\).  Hence
\[
D\setminus T=\varnothing
\qquad\text{and consequently}\qquad
D=T.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:arborescence}\), \(T\) is a rooted spanning arborescence, so the directed component \((V,D)\) is a rooted directed tree.  The definition of \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) imposes no restriction on \(B\) beyond being a bidirected edge set on \(V\); bows are therefore permitted.  Conversely, if \((V,D,B)\) is a mixed graph whose directed component is a rooted spanning arborescence, take \(T=D\) and any query \(e\in D\).  Then \(D\setminus T=\varnothing\), all the membership conditions in \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\) hold, and \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,0}\).  This proves the claimed equality of graph classes, with only the harmless change from the source's vertex labels \(\{0,\ldots,n\}\) to a set of cardinality \(n\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:gupta\mbox{-}blaser\mbox{-}tree\mbox{-}classification}\) to the queried coefficient \(\lambda_e\).  It returns either one generic coordinate value, two generic coordinate values, or infinitely many generic coordinate values, and in the finite cases its returned fractional affine square-root terms give all those values.

It remains to translate this solution-count trichotomy into the field degree in the present note.  By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), if \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\), its generic affine coordinate image over \(\overline{K_G}\) is exactly the root set of its monic minimal polynomial \(p_e\).  This polynomial is separable: indeed, \(K_G\) has characteristic zero, so \(p_e'\neq0\); irreducibility gives \(\gcd(p_e,p_e')=1\), because otherwise \(p_e\mid p_e'\), contrary to \(\deg p_e'<\deg p_e\).  Therefore \(p_e\) has exactly
\[
\deg p_e=[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]=d_e(G)
\]
distinct roots in \(\overline{K_G}\).  Thus one or two generic values imply, respectively, \(d_e(G)=1\) or \(d_e(G)=2\), and the returned terms \(\rho_i\) exhaust the roots.  If the published procedure reports infinitely many generic values, \(\lambda_e\) cannot be algebraic, since a nonzero polynomial has only finitely many roots; equivalently, the transcendental clause of \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) applies.  Hence \(d_e(G)=\infty\).  The cited procedure is randomized polynomial time and permits its polynomial-identity-test error to be set to any prescribed \(\eta\), completing the transfer.
